data.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
data.text: To demonstrate that 3 mg LY900018 is non-inferior to 1 mg IMG for the proportion of patients achieving treatment success from insulin-induced hypoglycemia using a non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Objective
data.text: To compare the safety and tolerability of 3 mg LY900018 with 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PK profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Objective
data.text: To characterize the PD profile of 3 mg LY900018 compared to 1 mg IMG

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Objective
data.text: Explore the formation of anti-glucagon antibodies to glucagon

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Recovery Objective
data.text: To evaluate the recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia

data.name: Primary Efficacy Endpoint
data.text: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in PG to >70 mg/dL or an increase of >20 mg/dL from nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Endpoint
data.text: SAE, TEAEs (including gastrointestinal, nasal, and non-nasal AEs), vital signs

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Endpoint
data.text: PK parameters include AUC, Cmax, Tmax

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Endpoint
data.text: PD parameters include BGmax and Tmax

data.name: Primary Efficacy Estimand: Non-inferiority of LY900018 vs IMG for Treatment Success
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who undergo controlled insulin-induced hypoglycemia and complete both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome. Patients are excluded if the lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, or if they receive an external measure to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration. (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods) Summary measure: Difference in proportions (percentage of treatment successes: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose before or within 10 minutes of glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives an external measure (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration either before glucagon administration or within the first 10 minutes of glucagon administration, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration (beyond the first 10 minutes) to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; data collected after IV glucose infusion may be excluded from efficacy analyses

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of both treatment periods
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study before completing both treatment periods with evaluable primary outcome for any reason (e.g., adverse event, withdrawal of consent, protocol deviation)

intercurrentEvents.name: Non-evaluable primary outcome due to insufficient hypoglycemia induction
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient's lowest PG concentration at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration is ≥70 mg/dL, indicating that adequate hypoglycemia was not achieved prior to glucagon dosing, rendering the primary outcome non-evaluable

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose by study site personnel versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection by study site personnel in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation, restricted to completers with evaluable primary outcome in both periods
data.variableOfInterest: The proportion of patients achieving treatment success defined as either an increase in plasma glucose (PG) to ≥70 mg/dL or an increase of ≥20 mg/dL from PG nadir within 30 minutes after administration of glucagon, without receiving additional treatments to increase PG. The nadir is defined as the minimum PG value at the time of or within 10 minutes following glucagon administration.
data.summaryMeasure: Difference in proportions (percentage of treatment successes: IMG minus LY900018) with a 2-sided 95% confidence interval derived from the 1-sample mean of paired differences in primary outcome across 2 treatment visits; non-inferiority declared if upper limit of 95% CI is less than the non-inferiority margin of 10%

data.name: Secondary Safety and Tolerability Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: All enrolled Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who received at least one dose of study treatment, regardless of whether they completed all protocol requirements (Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics including incidence rates (counts and percentages) of TEAEs and SAEs by treatment group; descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, range) for vital signs; summaries presented by severity and investigator-assessed relationship to investigational product.

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation due to adverse event
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues study participation due to an adverse event prior to completing both treatment periods

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of concomitant medications for hypoglycemia management
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives concomitant medications or interventions (e.g., IV glucose) to manage hypoglycemia or treat adverse events during the study period

intercurrentEvents.name: Pre-existing nasal or respiratory conditions
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has pre-existing nasal or respiratory symptoms that may confound assessment of nasal AEs attributed to LY900018

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Safety Population - all enrolled patients whether or not they completed all protocol requirements
data.variableOfInterest: Incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) including gastrointestinal AEs, nasal AEs, and non-nasal AEs; serious adverse events (SAEs); and changes in vital signs following single-dose administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics including incidence rates (counts and percentages) of TEAEs and SAEs by treatment group; descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, range) for vital signs; summaries presented by severity and investigator-assessed relationship to investigational product

data.name: Secondary Pharmacokinetic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation and have evaluable PK samples (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PK data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (geometric mean, coefficient of variation, median, range) for AUC and Cmax; median and range for Tmax; summarized by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or non-evaluable PK samples
intercurrentEvents.text: One or more scheduled PK blood samples are missing, hemolyzed, or otherwise non-evaluable, resulting in incomplete PK profiles

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion affecting glucagon PK assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion during the PK sampling window, potentially confounding glucagon concentration measurements

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before completion of PK sampling
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or is withdrawn before completion of the 4-hour post-dose PK sampling window

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PK data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacokinetic parameters derived from serial blood sampling for glucagon concentrations collected immediately before and up to 4 hours following glucagon administration, including area under the concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed concentration (Cmax), and time to maximum concentration (Tmax)
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (geometric mean, coefficient of variation, median, range) for AUC and Cmax; median and range for Tmax; summarized by treatment group

data.name: Secondary Pharmacodynamic Estimand: LY900018 vs IMG
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation and have evaluable PD (plasma glucose) data (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PD data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for BGmax and Tmax by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in plasma glucose values at various post-dose time points summarized descriptively.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives IV glucose infusion after glucagon administration to prevent progression to severe hypoglycemia; plasma glucose measurements taken after the time of IV glucose intervention will be excluded from PD analyses

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge
intercurrentEvents.text: All patients receive a carbohydrate-rich meal prior to discharge, which may affect plasma glucose measurements in the later post-dose period

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing or non-evaluable PD samples
intercurrentEvents.text: One or more scheduled plasma glucose samples are missing or non-evaluable, resulting in incomplete PD profiles

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection in a 2-period crossover design
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product according to treatment allocation with evaluable PD data
data.variableOfInterest: Pharmacodynamic parameters derived from serial plasma glucose measurements collected immediately before and up to 4 hours following glucagon administration, including maximum plasma glucose concentration (BGmax) and time to maximum plasma glucose concentration (Tmax)
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, maximum) for BGmax and Tmax by treatment group; absolute change from baseline in plasma glucose values at various post-dose time points summarized descriptively

data.name: Exploratory Anti-glucagon Antibody Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product and have evaluable antibody samples collected at screening and follow-up (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody data) Summary measure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline and post-dose follow-up; incidence of treatment-emergent anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Missing follow-up antibody sample
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not attend the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after last study treatment) or does not provide an evaluable blood sample for anti-glucagon antibody assessment

intercurrentEvents.name: Pre-existing anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient has detectable anti-glucagon antibodies at screening prior to any study treatment administration

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable anti-glucagon antibody data
data.variableOfInterest: Presence of anti-glucagon antibodies assessed at screening and at the follow-up visit (26 to 30 days after the last study treatment) to explore immunogenicity following single-dose glucagon administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive summary of the proportion of patients with detectable anti-glucagon antibodies at baseline and post-dose follow-up; incidence of treatment-emergent anti-glucagon antibodies by treatment group

data.name: Exploratory Hypoglycemia Symptoms Recovery Estimand
data.populationSummary: Japanese patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus who were randomized and received at least one dose of investigational product and completed the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire (Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale) at baseline and post-dose time points (Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data) Summary measure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, range) for total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline and post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline by treatment group.

intercurrentEvents.name: Receipt of additional intervention to raise plasma glucose
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient receives additional intervention (e.g., IV glucose infusion) to raise PG concentration, which may independently affect hypoglycemia symptom recovery independent of the study treatment effect

intercurrentEvents.name: Incomplete or missing questionnaire data
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient does not complete the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire at one or more scheduled post-dose time points due to inability to respond, early discharge, or other reasons

intercurrentEvents.name: Study discontinuation before post-dose symptom assessment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues the study or is withdrawn before completing post-dose hypoglycemia symptom assessments

data.treatment: 3 mg LY900018 (nasal glucagon) administered as a single nasal dose versus 1 mg intramuscular glucagon (IMG; GlucaGen, Novo Nordisk A/S) administered as a single IM injection
data.analysisPopulation: Full Analysis Set (FAS) - all randomized patients receiving at least one dose of investigational product with evaluable hypoglycemia symptom questionnaire data
data.variableOfInterest: Recovery from clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia assessed via the hypoglycemia symptoms questionnaire (Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale), including total score and each subscale score at baseline and various post-dose time points following glucagon administration
data.summaryMeasure: Descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, range) for total score and each subscale score of the Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Scale at baseline and post-dose time points, and absolute change from baseline by treatment group
